cancelAsk.text: The drive will be cleared and won't boot. Downloads already made are kept.
cancelAsk.title: Stop writing?
confirm.text: Everything on this {size} drive ({dev}) will be deleted and replaced with LordOS.
confirm.title: Erase {name}?
cooling.active-coolerHint: A heatsink with a fan on top.
cooling.case-fanHint: A case whose fan plugs into the board's fan header.
cooling.noneWarn: Under load it reaches 85 °C within minutes and throttles. A small heatsink or a fan makes a big difference.
cooling.noneWarnTitle: Without cooling the board slows itself down
cooling.overclockHint: 2.6 GHz instead of 2.4 GHz, with no extra voltage. Only with a fan.
cooling.overclockWarn: If the board doesn't start, open the card's boot partition on another computer and delete the lordos-firstrun block in config.txt.
cooling.overclockWarnTitle: Not every board is stable when overclocked
cooling.p.balancedHint: The fan starts at 55 °C and speeds up with the temperature. The default.
cooling.p.conservativeHint: A lower top clock (2.0 GHz) so the board stays cooler and doesn't throttle.
cooling.p.performanceHint: The fan starts earlier and the processor stays at its top clock.
cooling.p.quietHint: The fan starts later (60 °C). Fine for light use.
cooling.passiveHint: A metal case or heatsink, no fan.
cooling.text: What keeps your board cool? LordOS drives the fan by temperature and picks a profile to match.
cooling.unset: Not chosen: the board keeps its defaults.
custom.skipText: The board starts in setup mode: create your account in Settings → Users, then restart. Keep it off the network until then.
custom.text: Settings the board applies once when it starts for the first time. You can change everything later in Settings.
custom.title: Customise the first boot
custom.toggleOff: The board starts in setup mode and you create your account on it.
custom.toggleOn: Written to the card as a settings file that is deleted after it's applied.
device.pc.text: The live system on a USB stick: try LordOS and install it from there.
device.pc-arm64.text: The live system for UEFI arm64 machines on a USB stick: try LordOS and install it from there.
device.pcFooter: First-boot settings are for the Raspberry Pi; the live system asks for them while installing.
device.pcText: The PC image is the live system: it boots from the stick and can install LordOS on the computer's disk.
device.ram.max: Best performance, with room for everything.
device.ram.min: The minimum: it works, but heavy apps feel tight.
device.ramFooter: A fan (the active cooler or a case fan) and the 27 W power supply are recommended.
device.rpi5.text: BCM2712, 4 cores at 2.4 GHz. SD card or NVMe.
device.text: LordOS runs on the Raspberry Pi 5 and Pi 500 and on 64-bit PCs. Pick where this card or stick will be used.
device.title: Choose your device
done.ejected: {name} is ready and safe to remove.
done.notEjected: {name} is ready. Eject it before removing it.
done.pc1: Plug the stick into the PC
done.pc1Text: Turn it on and choose the USB drive in the boot menu (usually F12, F11, F8 or Esc).
done.pc2Text: The live system runs from the stick; Install LordOS puts it on the computer's disk.
done.pi1: Put the card in the Raspberry Pi 5
done.pi1Text: Connect a monitor, keyboard and mouse, then the power supply.
done.pi2Custom: It takes about a minute: the system grows to fill the card and applies your settings, then shows the login screen.
done.pi2Setup: It takes about a minute and starts in setup mode: create your account in Settings → Users.
done.pi3Text: From another computer at home it's {host}.
done.title: All done!
err.badSignature: The release signature doesn't match the LordOS key. Nothing was written.
err.hostChars: Use lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, not at the start or end (and not only numbers).
err.keyComment: The key's comment has invalid characters.
err.keyData: That doesn't look like a complete public key.
err.keyDss: DSA keys are no longer accepted. Create an ed25519 key.
err.keyRsaShort: RSA keys must have at least 2048 bits.
err.keyType: Not a supported key type (ed25519, ECDSA, security keys or RSA).
err.notListed: The signed list doesn't include this image. Nothing was written.
err.remoteNeedsUser: Remote desktop needs a user account.
err.sshNeedsKey: Add at least one key, or allow passwords.
err.ssidChars: The network name has an invalid character.
err.ssidLong: A network name has at most 32 bytes.
err.userChars: Start with a lowercase letter; then lowercase letters, numbers, _ or -.
err.userReserved: That name is reserved by the system.
err.wifiPassChars: Use plain letters, numbers and symbols (no accents) for a WPA2 password.
err.wifiPassLength: A Wi-Fi password has 8 to 63 characters.
err.zone: Choose a time zone from the list.
general.countryHint: Unlocks the radio channels allowed where you live.
general.hostnameHint: On your network it will be {name}.local. Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens.
image.customWarn: LordOS can't tell where it came from or whether someone changed it. It will be written and read back to check the copy, but only official images are verified. Use files you trust.
image.damaged: Its index can't be read, so its size is unknown. Download it again.
image.offlineText: Check the internet connection and try again, or use an image file you already have.
image.offlineTitle: The release list couldn't be fetched
image.staleText: The internet isn't reachable right now. Downloaded images still work: they are checked again before writing.
image.textPc: The latest LordOS live system for PCs, signed by the LordOS project, or an image file you already have.
image.textPi: The latest LordOS for the Raspberry Pi 5, signed by the LordOS project, or an image file you already have.
image.title: Choose a system image
look.theme.classicHint: A taskbar and a start menu.
look.theme.defaultHint: Menu bar at the top and the Dock.
more.bluetoothHint: Turn it off if you don't use it. Settings → Bluetooth turns it back on.
more.telemetry: LordOS collects nothing: no usage data, no crash reports, no accounts. The imager doesn't either.
more.updatesHint: Once a day LordOS fetches the signed update list and tells you when there's something new. It never installs on its own.
options.ejectHint: The drive can be removed right away.
options.followsSystem: Language and appearance follow LordOS (Settings → General and Appearance).
options.privacy: No telemetry: the imager only contacts the LordOS release page to list and download images.
options.title: App options
options.updateFound: LordOS Imager {v} is on the LordOS releases page.
options.updatesHint: Looks for a newer LordOS Imager in the LordOS release list it already reads. Nothing else is sent.
options.updatesSystem: The imager is part of LordOS: it's updated with the system.
profiles.name: Profile name
profiles.text: Save these settings to reuse them for the next card. Passwords and Wi-Fi keys are never saved: you type them again.
profiles.title: Customisation profiles
remote.addKeyHint: Paste the contents of a .pub file (for example ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub). Up to 16 keys.
remote.desktopFooter: Local network only, encrypted, and addresses that fail to log in 3 times are blocked. Change it in Settings → Sharing.
remote.desktopHint: From a browser on your local network: https://{host}.local:5673
remote.needUser: Remote access needs an account with a password (root never logs in). Add one in the User tab.
remote.passwordWarn: Keys only is recommended. With passwords, use a strong one and keep the board on your local network.
remote.sshText: A terminal on the board from another computer.
review.checkCustom: Reading the drive back (the file itself isn't signed)
review.checkOfficial: Release signature, SHA-256, and reading the drive back
review.text: Check that everything is right. The drive is erased when you confirm.
review.title: Ready to write
storage.bigText: {size} is unusual for an SD card or a USB stick. Make sure it isn't a backup disk.
storage.eraseText: All {size} of it, every partition and every file. This can't be undone.
storage.hidden: Internal disks and the disk this computer runs from are never shown.
storage.hiddenSome: Internal disks and the disk this computer runs from are never shown ({n} hidden).
storage.inUse: In use: {names}. It will be unmounted.
storage.noneText: Insert an SD card (with a card reader if needed) or plug in a USB drive. It appears here by itself.
storage.noneTitle: No card or USB drive found
storage.readOnly: Write-protected: slide the card's lock switch.
storage.text: The SD card or USB drive LordOS will be written to.
storage.title: Choose the storage
storage.tooLargeMbr: Larger than 2 TiB: LordOS images can't use a drive this big (and it isn't a card or a stick).
storage.tooSmallPc: Too small: use a drive of at least 2 GB.
storage.tooSmallPi: Too small: use a card of at least 8 GB (16 GB or more is better).
subtitle: SD cards and USB sticks
tip.cancelled.text: The drive was cleared. Try again whenever you like; the download is kept.
tip.cancelled.title: Stopped, all safe
tip.custom.text: Nobody vouches for this one: I can check that it's written correctly, not where it came from.
tip.custom.title: A file of your own
tip.customise.text: Set it up now and the board starts with your account, network and look. Nothing secret is stored in clear.
tip.customise.title: Ready on the first boot
tip.device.text: I'll walk you through it. Pick the computer the card is for; I'll only offer what LordOS really supports.
tip.device.title: Hi, I'm Lumo!
tip.erase.text: Copy anything you want to keep first. Writing erases the whole drive.
tip.erase.title: Everything on it goes
tip.failed.text: The drive was cleared so it doesn't look half-written. You can try again.
tip.failed.title: That didn't work
tip.image.text: Official images are checked against the LordOS release key before anything is erased. I keep the download, so the next card is quicker.
tip.image.title: Only signed images
tip.storage.text: Only SD cards and USB drives show up here. The disk this computer runs from is never offered.
tip.storage.title: Plug in your card
tip.tab.cooling.text: With a fan, the board can stay at full speed. Without one, a gentler clock avoids throttling.
tip.tab.cooling.title: Keep it cool
tip.tab.general.text: The computer name is how you'll reach it: name.local from any computer at home.
tip.tab.general.title: Find it on the network
tip.tab.look.text: You can change all of this later in Settings → Appearance.
tip.tab.look.title: Make it yours
tip.tab.more.text: LordOS collects nothing about you. Not now, not later.
tip.tab.more.title: Nothing leaves the board
tip.tab.remote.text: SSH with keys only can't be guessed. Remote desktop stays on your local network.
tip.tab.remote.title: Keys are safer
tip.tab.user.text: Your password is turned into a one-way hash right before writing. A long sentence makes a great password.
tip.tab.user.title: Only a hash goes on the card
tip.tab.wifi.text: I store the network's derived key, not the password you type.
tip.tab.wifi.title: No Wi-Fi password on the card
tip.untouched.text: The drive is as it was. Read what happened and try again.
tip.untouched.title: Nothing was touched
tip.write.text: Look over the summary. After you confirm, the drive is erased and written.
tip.write.title: Last check
tip.writing.text: Don't remove the drive. I'll read everything back to be sure it's right.
tip.writing.title: On it!
title: LordOS Imager
unavailable.text: It needs LordOS's administration helper, which isn't available in this session.
unavailable.title: The imager can't run here
user.autologinHint: Starts the desktop without asking for the password. Anyone who turns it on gets your session.
user.hashNote: Only a yescrypt or SHA-512 hash of the password is written to the card, never the password.
user.intro: An administrator account for you. Root stays locked; the setup account is removed.
user.name: User name
user.nameHint: Lowercase letters, numbers, _ and -. You'll log in with it.
wifi.enableHint: The board joins this network on its first boot.
wifi.ethernet: Without Wi-Fi, plug in an Ethernet cable: the board gets its address by itself.
wifi.hiddenHint: The network doesn't announce its name.
wifi.noRadio: This computer has no Wi-Fi radio to scan with. Type the network name.
wifi.openWarn: Prefer a network with a password.
wifi.openWarnTitle: Anyone nearby can see open-network traffic
wifi.pskNote: The card stores the network's derived WPA2 key, not your password. A WPA3-only network needs the password itself: enter it on the board in Settings → Network.
write.cancelledText: The drive was cleared. Nothing else was changed.
write.failedText: The drive was cleared so it doesn't look half-written.
write.text: Keep the drive plugged in. This takes a few minutes.
write.title: Writing to {name}
write.untouchedText: Nothing on the drive was changed.
general.langSince: {name} needs a LordOS {v} image or newer.
err.langImage: This image can’t start in that language: choose English, Español or Português, or a newer image.
device.piNext: Next you choose the model. They use the same LordOS image; the model sets the right tips and the cooling options.
device.modelText: Both use the same LordOS image. Choosing the model shows the right tips and checks.
device.rpi500.text: 8 GB · a Pi 5 inside a keyboard. SD card or USB drive.
device.rpi500.note: 8 GB is comfortable for daily use. Use the official 27 W power supply. It has no fan: a large heatsink inside keeps it cool.
cooling.noFan: The Raspberry Pi 500 has no fan header: a large heatsink inside keeps it cool. Choose the profile; LordOS shows its temperature in Settings → Cooling.
cooling.p.balancedPassiveHint: The processor keeps its full clock (2.4 GHz); if it gets too hot, the board slows down by itself. The default.
